body.p: JALv3 provides three text conversion casts and the COUNT operator. Both are ordinary operators of the language: they may be used wherever a value is expected, including comparisons, concatenations, and procedure arguments.

section.title: Text conversion casts
section.p: STRING(x) renders an integer in decimal, or copies the bytes of a byte array as characters. HEX(x) renders a value in lowercase hexadecimal without a prefix, and BIN(x) does the same in binary. For both, an optional second argument sets a minimum number of digits, so HEX(26, 4) is "001a" and BIN(5, 8) is "00000101"; a value that needs more digits renders at its full width. For arrays, each element is rendered at its natural width, and HEX zero-pads each byte element to two digits.
section.codeblock: CONST STRING S1 = string(26) -- "26" CONST STRING S2 = hex(26) -- "1a" CONST STRING S3 = hex(26, 4) -- "001a" CONST STRING S4 = bin(5) -- "101" CONST STRING S5 = bin(5, 8) -- "00000101" CONST BYTE TBL[3] = {1, 2, 3} CONST STRING S6 = string(TBL) -- the three bytes as characters CONST STRING S7 = hex(TBL) -- "010203"
section.p: Constant operands are folded into read-only memory at compile time, so the examples above need no heap. Runtime operands are rendered when the program runs, through the string machinery described in , and therefore need the string heap:
section.codeblock:
CONST WORD _string_heap_size = 64 VAR STRING out VAR BYTE cnt = 26
out = "hex=" & hex(cnt, 4) -- "hex=001a" IF string(cnt) == "26" THEN ... END IF
section.p: The result is an ordinary string value: it can be compared with literals and composed in concatenation chains. The names STRING, HEX, and BIN followed by an opening parenthesis always denote the cast, even if a symbol of the same name exists.

section.title: COUNT
section.p: COUNT reports the size of its operand. What is counted depends on the kind of operand:

row.entry: array variable, or fixed-size array formal
the number of elements passed by the caller

section.codeblock:
VAR BYTE arr[10] VAR QWORD wide VAR STRING msg = "hello"
COUNT(arr) -- 10 COUNT(wide) -- 8 COUNT(msg) -- 5 (current length) COUNT(arr[0]) -- 1 (a byte)
section.p: COUNT is computed at compile time whenever the operand is static, and at run time for dynamic strings and open-array formals. The older _length(expr) operator is still accepted; with -warn-misc the compiler suggests COUNT instead.
